newsitem.title: INDIA: Erratic rains delay oilseeds sowing in India.
newsitem.headline: Erratic rains delay oilseeds sowing in India.

text.p: Oilseeds sowing in India has been delayed due to heavy rain and waterlogging in western areas and deficient rains in southern states, industry officials said on Monday.
They said groundnut sowing in the western state of Gujarat was expected to be delayed at least 10 days due to waterlo gged fields.

Navinbhai Shah, president of Bombay Oilseeds and Oil Exchange said sowing in Gujara would now be possible only in the second week of July as it would take more than a week for fields to dry out. Sowing normally starts at the end of June.
Gujarat produces nearly 35 percent of the country's groundnut output.
More than 100 people have died in Gujarat over the past eight days in floods triggered by torrential monsoon rains.
Shah said sowing had started in some areas in the state's Saurashtra region but seeds were washed away in heavy rain, adding, "the damage is only marginal."
Industry officials said rainfall was gradually increasing in oilseed regions in the southern states of Karnataka and Andhra Pradesh but was still too light for sowing to start.

Traders and industry officials said soybean sowing on about 55,000 hectares in the Indore region of the central state of Madhya Pradesh was over but rainfall was insufficient in other soybean-growing areas.
"Rainfall in central India is not sufficient in all areas," Shah said. Madhya Pradesh produces about 80 percent of Indian soybeans.
Industry officials said rice sowing was in full swing in all states after monsoon rains covered most regions.
"Rains in most rice-growing regions are on schedule," said Tarun Kumar, an official in a leading New Delhi foodgrains export firm. --Sambit Mohanty, New Delhi newsroom +91-11 301 2024
